chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them).

Regarding a man who says to his slave: 'I free you on the condition that I marry you to my daughter; if you marry her or take her as a concubine, then one hundred dinars are due upon you.' He frees him under that condition, and the slave either marries her or takes her as a concubine. He (the Imam) said: 'One hundred dinars are due upon him.'

key_terms.دِينَار: A gold coin, used here as a unit of currency for the penalty
key_terms.عِتْق: Manumission or freeing of a slave

ai.seo_question: What is the legal consequence if a slave is freed on the condition of marrying his master's daughter and that condition is met?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the financial liability in conditional manumission (*itq*), establishing that the penalty of one hundred dinars is triggered specifically upon the fulfillment of the marriage or concubinage condition. It reflects the juristic principle that such conditions create a binding debt (*daman*) on the freed slave, illustrating the practical application of manumission contracts in early Shia legal theory.
